title: How NVIDIA Minerva Turns Telemetry Chaos Into Peak GPU Yield | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform that unifies telemetry across GPUs, networking and storage into a knowledge graph tied to active jobs, so it can find gray failures, collapse alert storms into single incidents and let operators query root causes through an agent called Sherlock. NVIDIA says it saved hundreds to thousands of GPU hours in cited cases, including 54 hours of cluster uptime for one 81-event incident.

themes.theme: Why AI factories break conventional monitoring

insights.claim: In synchronous distributed training a job advances at the pace of its slowest rank, so a single degraded GPU, interface, storage device or switch path can waste time across many healthy resources.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: At cluster scale a small fault multiplies into large GPU-hour losses, so reliability tooling bears directly on return on GPU investment.
insights.quote: In synchronous distributed training, a job advances at the pace of its slowest rank.
insights.locator: AI Factories are some of the most technologically complex

insights.claim: Damaging failures are often subtle: a GPU a few degrees hotter than its peers, an NVMe drive that slows only under sustained load, or a pause-frame storm that looks like many unrelated symptoms. None of them necessarily crosses a static threshold, but together they cause stragglers, longer step times and delayed checkpoints.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: Threshold-based monitoring misses a main loss mechanism in large training clusters.
insights.locator: The failures that hurt yield are often subtle

insights.claim: Evidence is split across teams: network operators see interface counters, compute operators see GPU health and ML teams see step times, so each view is accurate but the relationships stay hidden. Triage then becomes dashboard searches and handoffs that can turn a contained fault into hours or days of lost production.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: The gap is organizational as well as technical, which supports a unified cross-stack product.
insights.quote: Triage becomes a chain of dashboard searches and cross-team handoffs
insights.locator: Diagnosis becomes harder because the evidence is split

insights.claim: Rule-based monitoring assumes a known metric crossing a known boundary signals a known condition, and it struggles with "gray failures" where a component stays available and the problem shows only under load or against peers. Aggressive thresholds add false warnings during normal workload changes.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: This is the case for peer-relative ML detection over static rules.
insights.quote: Rule-based monitoring assumes that a known metric crossing a known boundary indicates a known condition.
insights.locator: Why conventional monitoring breaks at AI factory scale

insights.claim: One physical fault can produce interface errors, RX pause frames, congestion, GPU utilization changes and slower jobs, and separate dashboards present these as unrelated events (alert amplification). For operations the workload is the unit that matters: teams need to know which job is affected and where its resources sit.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: Alert tooling that is not workload- and topology-aware adds noise at scale.
insights.quote: For operations, the workload is the unit that matters.

themes.theme: Minerva architecture: knowledge graph and ML detection

insights.claim: NVIDIA Minerva ingests metrics, logs and topology from GPUs, Spectrum-X and NVLink switches, SuperNICs, DPUs, storage, NCCL, schedulers and AI workloads. It auto-discovers relationships to build a knowledge graph that updates as the environment changes and can span multiple data centers.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: The product pulls observability across NVIDIA's own hardware stack into a single layer, deepening platform lock-in.
insights.locator: Solving these challenges requires end-to-end visibility

insights.claim: Minerva processes billions of metric and log data points per hour with supervised models for known critical errors and unsupervised models that learn normal behavior per component and compare it with peers. Multivariate models combine temperature, power, clocks, utilization and workload state to detect degradation before outright failure.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: Peer comparison is the key technique for catching degradation that stays within specification.
insights.quote: Peer comparison matters because a measurement can look acceptable in isolation and still be anomalous in context.
insights.locator: Detecting gray failures with purpose-built machine learning

insights.claim: Topology-aware correlation uses the knowledge graph to group events that share a dependency path into one incident. NVIDIA reports significant reductions in notified events and tickets, but operators still need other Minerva capabilities to find the root cause, though with a much smaller search space.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: The claim is qualitative apart from the anecdotes, and it stops short of fully automated root-cause analysis.

insights.claim: A native agent called Sherlock, grounded in live telemetry and the knowledge graph, lets operators ask in natural language why a job slowed, and an MCP server exposes the same context to external agentic tools. Mitigation can stay human-approved or selected actions can be automated according to local policy and risk.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: Operational context is being packaged as an agent interface, which pushes junior operators toward self-service on tasks that used to need specialists.
insights.quote: This gives less experienced operators a route to domain knowledge that has traditionally required escalation to a specialist.

themes.theme: Reported case studies and yield gains

insights.claim: Anomaly detection found one NVLink connection, out of roughly 400,000 interfaces, that was quietly losing bandwidth and linked its switch to the affected training jobs. The SRE drained and rescheduled nodes and diagnosed the problem in minutes instead of hours.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: A single degraded link can slow a whole job, which is why fleet-wide detection pays off.
insights.quote: Anomaly detection found the one NVLink connection out of roughly 400,000 interfaces that was quietly losing bandwidth.

insights.claim: Rare-log anomaly detection flagged a never-before-seen PCIe-level APEI hardware error on a node's SuperNIC path, and the node was removed from the allocation pool before customer workloads landed on it, saving hundreds of GPU hours.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: Proactive node draining converts a latent fault into avoided lost compute.

insights.claim: Minerva traced slow training jobs to an NVMe device that could not wake from a low-power state, which caused I/O write errors on every job on that host. Draining the node and returning the drive for RMA saved an estimated 5,530 hours of job runtime.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: One failed storage device had a large and non-obvious impact on cluster-wide runtime.
insights.quote: The fix saved an estimated 5,530 hours of job runtime.
insights.locator: Straggler job due to NVMe power fault

insights.claim: A switch page-fault restart set off a congestion cascade of RX pause frames, repeated link downs and GPU anomalies, producing as many as 81 noisy events. Minerva grouped them into a single incident for the affected job, cutting repair time and saving about 54 hours of total cluster uptime.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: Event correlation reduces mean time to repair in cascading network faults.
insights.quote: Handling it as one incident instead of 81 cut time to repair and saved about 54 hours of total cluster uptime.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's internal testing shows higher mean time between interrupts through proactive maintenance, lower mean time to repair through automated root-cause analysis and much less alert noise, which together raise effective GPU hours. No figures are given and the testing is NVIDIA's own.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: The yield claim is directional and unquantified, so independent confirmation is needed.
insights.locator: Turning operational gains into useful compute

insights.claim: Minerva is being aligned with NVIDIA DSX OS and reuses selected DSX OS health and resilience components such as NVIDIA Attribution. Starting with the data collector, Minerva capabilities will become open-source parts of DSX OS, giving a modular telemetry base aligned with NVIDIA reference architectures.
insights.speaker: Rahul Aggarwal
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is building its own AI-factory operating stack and open-sourcing the collector to spread adoption of its telemetry standard.
insights.quote: NVIDIA Minerva capabilities beginning with the data collector will become open-source parts of DSX OS.
